transcript:
Header: Date: 2025-05-06 | Start: 16:00 PST | Duration: 42 mins
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lina Ho (Redwood CSM); Karen Lee (AcmeFin ML Eng), Jamal Owens (Product), Priya Nair (Security), Ethan Cho (Data)

Summary (auto): quick pass over last week's evaluation, a few regressions flagged on QA prompts, narrowed down to prompt drift after the token-window change, discussion of guardrails and pilot next steps.

00:00 Samira: okay hey everyone, thanks for joining. Can you all hear me?
00:05 Karen: yep, good here.
00:08 Diego: yeah good, sorry on a little delay traffic.
00:15 Samira: quick agenda, we'll run through the latest quality eval spreadsheet, look at the 3 regressions Karen called out, talk guardrails and mitigation, then next steps and timing.
00:28 Jamal: sounds good. we especially want to avoid the hallucination cases from last week.
00:33 Samira: right right. Diego do you want to pull up the eval?
00:36 Diego: pulling it up now, lemme share my screen. okay spreadsheet v3 is open, columns are prompt_id, category, expected, model_response, score, notes. some transcription notes, the automated scorer uses embedding-sim and nli, plus human spot checks.
00:54 Karen: I like that mix, embedding sim plus NLI caught the majority but two cases slipped through.
01:02 Diego: first regression is prompt_142, that was fine last week but now the model truncates the second bullet causing missing context. we suspect sequence-window config changed after Diego: our last kernel selection tweak — sorry I mean last runtime patch.
01:22 Lina: (laughs) Diego live debugging.
01:25 Diego: yeah, so we have a subtle tokenization cutoff after 1024 window for that model variant; Redwood Optimize suggested the quant profile which changed the padding behavior, so KV cache behavior slightly different — sometimes shows as "KV cash" in logs, which is annoying but it's the same thing.
01:44 Priya: just to flag, if we move to Dedicated pilot we need KMS integration and audit log retention to meet our compliance.
01:52 Samira: totally, we can share our SOC 2 and the private deployment checklist. I'll attach the security docs after.
01:58 Priya: and SSO — we need SAML+SCIM for user provisioning.
02:03 Samira: yes, SAML and SCIM supported. Diego will follow up on the KMS key rotation questions.
02:10 Diego: noted.
02:12 Jamal: back to regressions, prompt_198 is a semantics error where the model hallucinates a statute citation. that's a big no for compliance.
02:22 Diego: yeah that one looks like the model is overconfident on low-support facts. We can tighten guardrails by adding more negative examples in the prompt set and a strict citation requirement. also could run a retrieval check before generation.
02:35 Karen: retrieval is nice but adds latency; can we do a hybrid where we only retrieve on flagged categories?
02:42 Diego: yes, policy routing could send certain categories to a retrieval-enhanced path, Redwood Console supports per-route settings. there might be a small latency bump but cost's manageable.
02:55 Samira: and we can A/B the retrieval route to measure impact on QA accuracy vs latency.
03:02 Ethan: what's the baseline latency we saw last week on the sample?
03:06 Diego: median token latency was 12ms on hosted, on the dedicated pool we saw 9-10ms median, but tail worsened under burst. the regression test here runs 5k prompts, average end-to-end was 480ms for full responses.
03:24 Karen: ok so dedicated improves median but there's some tail. could autoscale help?
03:28 Samira: yes configurable autoscaling and burst pools. I'll include options in the pricing.
03:34 Jamal: any idea of cost delta for enabling retrieval per-request?
03:38 Diego: depends on docs size and retrieval hits; rough estimate is +15-30% token/cpu cost. we'll model that in the spreadsheet.
03:47 03:48 Samira: next regression, prompt_210 — model ignored guardrail about financial advice, gave prescriptive steps. That one triggered Priya.
03:58 Priya: yeah it's risky. We need hard block on prescriptive advices, and audit trail for every such block.
04:05 Diego: we can implement a pre-check classifier that tags any 'advice' intent with high confidence and returns a canned safe-response or escalation. Redwood has an internal template for that, we can ship as a prompt + policy.
04:17 Karen: will that increase false positives?
04:20 Diego: maybe a bit, but we can tune thresholds and human-review fallback. also show confidence scores in the response metadata so you can trace why a response was blocked.
04:33 Lina: side note, the transcript shows a few typos in the automatic transcription, sometimes 'Redwood Dedicated' becomes 'Redwood dedicat ed' in the logs, so when Diego references logs he means the runtime traces.
04:45 Diego: yep, apologies, voice to text is rough.
04:47 Jamal: fine. so what's the plan for the prompt set?
04:50 Samira: Karen, you mentioned you had 50 new edge cases?
04:54 Karen: yes, I uploaded them to the shared drive this morning under eval/prompts/edgecases_v2. they focus on hallucinations and sensitive financial guidance.
05:02 Diego: perfect, I'll include them in the regression suite. can you also add expected-citation fields? that helps automated scoring.
05:10 Karen: will do.
05:12 Samira: quick check on scoring, currently embedding-sim threshold at 0.78, NLI pass if not contradicted, human spot-check at 10% sample. should we tighten emb-sim to 0.82 for finance category?
05:25 Diego: that would reduce false accepts but may increase false rejects; for finance I think higher precision is worth it. we can tune per-category.
05:34 Jamal: can we get per-prompt historic trend lines in Redwood Console? last week I couldn't find the time-series.
05:41 Lina: console should have it under model -> routes -> metrics. Diego, any thoughts what we need to enable?
05:49 Diego: you need to enable eval retention and tie the prompt_id to the route. I'll send steps. Samira: we'll set up a dashboard for AcmeFin.
05:58 Samira: next topic: regression run cadence and thresholds. how many false positives/negatives acceptable?
06:06 Karen: for now zero hallucinations that reference regulations; for other categories we can accept up to 2% false negatives on a 5k run.
06:15 Diego: noted. I'll run a 5k and flag any that reference legal/regulatory text — we'll return exact matches and similarity scores.
06:25 Priya: on audit logs, how long do you retain request+response?
06:29 Samira: default 90 days; enterprise can extend with retention add-on. We'll document options.
06:35 Priya: we need 1 year for a subset of redacted audits.
06:39 Samira: ok we'll confirm retention SLAs in the security docs.
06:43 06:44 Jamal: are there any new regressions besides the three?
06:46 Diego: there's a small uptick in hallucinated entity linking on prompts that rely on external tables — likely due to tokenization change mentioned earlier. that's item four in the sheet.
06:57 Karen: can we run a debug with full kv dump?
07:00 Diego: we can but privacy concerns — we'd redact PII. we can share aggregated KV stats and mismatch traces.
07:10 Samira: Diego will produce an anonymized trace.
07:13 Diego: yes I'll scrub PII and share a condensed log.
07:17 Ethan: what's the format you prefer for logs?
07:20 Diego: csv for the KV mismatch and a short jsonl for per-request metadata — sorry that might sound technical in the transcript, but we'll attach both.
07:31 Samira: next, pilot plan: we propose 3-week canary in dedicated with A/B guardrail on route. measure QA accuracy, latency, cost. Diego to propose exact run.
07:45 Diego: proposed config: baseline route on hosted, variant on dedicated with retrieval on flagged categories, 10% traffic to variant ramping to 50% if safe. rollback policy on 2 consecutive regression alerts.
07:59 Jamal: that rollback policy is good. how are alerts triggered?
08:03 Diego: we have automated eval pipelines that compute weekly aggregate and trigger if regression rate exceeds threshold or if a heavy failure occurs (e.g., hallucination referencing regulation).
08:15 Karen: what about human-in-loop review?
08:18 Samira: we'll set a 24-hour review window for flagged items where a reviewer can mark false positives.
08:24 Priya: make sure reviewers are auditable and we capture who marked what.
08:28 Lina: CSM note: we can include reviewer emails in audit trail.
08:32 08:33 Samira: timeline wise, Diego will run the 5k regression this week, share logs; Samira will send pricing and security docs; Karen will add prompts and expected citations; Priya will provide final compliance checklist. schedule canary next Tues if all good.
08:49 Jamal: Tuesday next week works.
08:52 Samira: quick Q: are we good to enable dedicated test nodes for Diego tomorrow?
08:56 Karen: yeah let's do it.
08:58 Diego: I'll provision them, might be a short window for kernel/quant differences.
09:04 09:05 Samira: any blockers?
09:06 Priya: None beyond finalizing KMS and retention which we discussed.
09:10 Samira: cool. recap please, Lina?
09:13 Lina: recap: Diego run 5k regression and anonymized KV traces, Samira share security & pricing, Karen update prompts with citations, Priya confirm SSO/KMS requirements, schedule canary next Tue and prepare dashboard in Redwood Console.
09:30 Karen: thanks all.
09:32 Samira: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in thread.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcription had some name swaps and tokenization references came across oddly (KV cash, dediacted). Minor fillers and overlaps present.

References/Artifacts shared: https://drive.redwood/example/evals/edgecases_v2 (Karen's uploads), https://redwood/docs/security/ (security checklist), Eval spreadsheet: /shared/evals/acmefin_weekly_v3.xlsx

End of transcript.
